To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the existing techniques for exploiting soft and hard correlations in relational databases are not suitable for big data infrastructures because the optimization factors are different, 2) the correlations among attributes of big data are not only soft but also hard and can be exploited in query optimization in a systematic manner, 3) the correlations can be discovered by using a new technique called Correlation Discovery (CD), which is a novel technique to discover the correlations among attributes by exploiting the fact that they have been stored

(1) the existing techniques for exploiting soft and hard correlations in relational databases are not applicable to big-data systems; (2) the soft and hard correlations are very important in big-data systems, and their systematic exploitation in query optimization is crucial; and (3) the soft and the hard correlations can be effectively exploited to optimize the performance of big data query processing.

(1) we have proposed a new framework for discovering, validating, and exploiting soft correlations in big data infrastructions and (2) our experimental evaluation shows that the new framework is effective in improving query performance by up to 2.5x.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: How can we discover and utilize soft correlations to optimize queries? How can we utilize hard correlations to optimize queries?

the following three research questions: (i) How to discover soft correlations in big datasets and how to validate them? (ii) How to exploit soft and hard correlations in query optimization of big data infrastructures? (iii) How to design a system that supports the above two research questions?

the following two problems: (1) How to discover soft and hard correlations from big data and validate their worthiness for query optimization? (2) How to exploit the discovered correlations in query optimization?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no effective techniques for exploiting soft and hard correlations in big data query optimization.
there is no systematic and efficient approach for exploiting correlations in big data infra- structures.

the state of the art of query optimization techniques for big data infrastructures is still in its infancy, and there is a need for a new generation of query optimization techniques that would be tailored towards big data infrastructures and their unique characteristics, and would exploit the soft and hard correlations in the datasets to optimize the query execution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a framework for exploiting correlations among attributes in big data query optimization.

we have proposed a novel approach, called SoftCor, to exploit soft correlations in big data query optimization, in which we have developed a novel technique, called SoftCor-Index, for indexing soft correlations and a novel technique, SoftCor-Optimizer, for exploiting them in query optimization, which has been implemented as a Hadoop plug-in.
we have proposed a novel framework for exploiting soft and hard correlations in Hadoop, which is a first attempt to address this issue in the big data context.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, with the help of a new data property called soft correlation, we can discover and utilize correlations in big data query optimization, and achieve significant performance improvement over the current state of the art.
, in big data query optimization, the soft correlations among attributes are as important as the hard ones.

the existing approaches for exploiting correlations in query optimization, e.g., CORDS, BHUNT, and CM, do not apply in Hadoop, because of the differences between Hadoop and RDBMSs in terms of the data model and query execution.
